tech.intro: Gofer turns real-world task recordings into structured motion data — the fuel that teaches physical AI to operate in the real world.
tech.step1Body: Vision AI breaks each video into discrete action primitives — reach, grasp, move, place — with timestamps and confidence scores.
tech.step2Body: Videos are embedded into a vector space. Researchers query in plain language to find matching demonstrations across the entire dataset instantly.
tech.step3Body: Action sequences become robot-ready output — motion trajectories and task graphs compatible with standard robotics frameworks.
tech.researchSubtitle: Built on the frontier of imitation learning and embodied AI.
tech.r1Body: Robots trained on real human demonstrations generalise far better than those trained on synthetic data. Gofer provides the demonstration scale that makes this possible.
tech.r2Body: Gofer converts raw video into structured action data — hand pose, keypoints, interaction graphs — ready for embodied AI systems to train policies.
tech.r3Body: Real-world recordings capture diversity that synthetic data can't — varied lighting, surfaces, and technique. That breadth is exactly what robots need in deployment.
tech.r4Title: From Real-World Work to Frontier Labs
tech.r4Body: Captured tasks are licensed to robotics labs, AI companies, and universities. Organizations participate in the value created when their data is licensed.

howitworks.intro: Gofer bridges the gap between human skill and robotic execution by turning real-world task videos into structured, machine-readable motion data — the fuel that teaches physical AI to operate in the real world.
howitworks.step1Body: Multimodal vision AI analyzes each captured video frame-by-frame, identifying discrete action primitives — reach, grasp, move, place, release — along with the objects and surfaces involved. Each action is timestamped and classified with confidence scores.
howitworks.step2Body: Every analyzed video is embedded into a high-dimensional vector space using multimodal encoders. Researchers and robotics teams can query the dataset in natural language — finding semantically similar demonstrations across thousands of recordings instantly.
howitworks.step3Body: Detected action sequences are converted into canonical robot-executable representations — motion trajectories, joint-space commands, and task graphs — compatible with standard robotics frameworks used in labs and industry.
howitworks.researchIntro: Gofer is built on foundational advances in embodied AI, imitation learning, and robot manipulation research.
howitworks.r1Body: Modern robotic systems struggle to generalize to unstructured real-world environments because they lack exposure to the diversity of how humans actually perform tasks. Imitation learning — training robots directly from human demonstrations — has emerged as the most promising path to dexterous, general-purpose robots. Gofer provides the large-scale, high-quality demonstration data that makes this possible.
howitworks.r2Body: Embodied AI research focuses on agents that perceive, reason, and act in the physical world. Gofer's pipeline converts raw video into structured action data that embodied AI systems can directly consume — from hand pose and skeletal keypoints to object interaction graphs and canonical action traces — enabling researchers to train and evaluate policies at scale.
howitworks.r3Body: Synthetic data and lab recordings capture only a narrow slice of real-world task variation. Human-recorded videos from everyday environments capture the full diversity of surfaces, lighting conditions, object states, and individual technique that robots must handle in deployment. Gofer's partner organizations generate this diversity at a scale no individual lab can replicate.
howitworks.r4Title: From Real-World Work to Frontier Labs
howitworks.r4Body: Captured tasks are processed, labeled, and packaged into structured datasets licensed to robotics labs, frontier AI companies, universities, and enterprise customers for internal research, training, evaluation, and benchmarking. Organizations share in the value created when their data is licensed.
